app.stack: next.js / tRPC over Next.js route handlers

backend.note: there is also a REST API under apps/api, versioned separately

apiDocs.note: tRPC procedures with Zod input schemas — the payload shapes are readable directly.

notes: 78 routes are declared. Only the public booker is reachable without an account, so the crawl covers 2 of them and every other route lands in app-model.json as crawled:false. That asymmetry is why this app is in the corpus.
Route groups in parentheses — (booking-page-wrapper), (use-page-wrapper) — organise files and do not appear in the URL.
An optional catch-all segment ([[...step]]) resolves to the URL without it, the same rule an optional group follows in a hash router.

labelAssociation.note: Labels are properly associated, so getByLabel works — the only corpus app where it does. Where a control has no label, data-testid is present and is the better handle anyway.

notes: This app needs the least from the label machinery and the most from the route union: it is the case where 'a declared route the crawl never reached is still a page object' does the real work.

spec.title: Cal.diy API v2
spec.note: A full OpenAPI 3 document sits in the clone. The tRPC surface under packages/trpc is separate and serves the web app; this REST API is the documented, versioned one and is what a precondition should use.

auth.specSays: nothing — the document declares no securitySchemes, no top-level security and no per-operation security, so which credential each endpoint wants is not stated by the contract.

loginEndpoint.note: this is the web app's NextAuth session login, read from source. It authenticates the UI, not necessarily this REST API.

auth.note: Do not assume a bearer token or an API key here: the spec does not say, and nothing in this corpus can call the API to find out. Settle it against a self-hosted deployment before writing a precondition.

authVerification.reason: the spec declares no security scheme — settle the credential against a deployment first

controls.name: How much does Cal.com cost and what's included in each plan?Cal.com's free plan includes unlimited event types, calendar syncing, workflow automation, Stripe payments, and Cal Video, making it one of the most fully featured free scheduling tools on the market. For teams, the booking software scales across four tiers. Teams ($16/user/month) adds round-robin scheduling, shared availability, and team workflows, making it ideal scheduling software for small business. Organizations ($37/user/month) include org-wide admin controls and centralized management for larger companies using Cal.com’s scheduler as their meeting scheduling software. Enterprise offers custom pricing with priority support, dedicated database, and higher SLAs. This is crucial for industries that require a secure online booking system.

What are Cal.com's pricing plans, and is it good scheduling software for small businesses?Cal.com is one of the best options for scheduling software for small business thanks to a free tier that includes unlimited event types, workflow automation, Stripe payments, and Cal Video, making it the most generous free scheduling tool available. Small businesses needing booking software with team features can upgrade to Teams at $16/user/month for round-robin scheduling and shared availability. It also works as an online booking system for small businesses with embeddable booking pages. Organizations ($37/user/month) adds admin controls for mid-size to large companies. Enterprise offers custom pricing with priority support, dedicated database, and higher SLAs. The enterprise plan features are crucial for industries that require a secure meeting scheduling software with a secure database.

Can Cal.com be used as scheduling software for Healthcare, Sales, Support, and B2B teams?Yes. Cal.com adapts as scheduling software across industries and team structures. Healthcare practices use it as patient scheduling software and physician scheduling software with HIPAA compliance, SOC 2 Type II certification, and encrypted storage. Thanks to the flexibility of Cal.com it is widely used by sales teams across industries. Support teams use the round-robin scheduling feature of Cal.com to fairly distribute workload among team members. For B2B sales teams, Cal.com works as booking software with attribute-based routing, round-robin lead distribution, and CRM updates in Salesforce or HubSpot on every booking. It's a complete automated scheduling system, online booking system, and scheduler for any vertical.

controls.name: How does Cal.com differ from other scheduling tools?Cal.com was built for organizations, not individuals. It combines enterprise-grade security (SSO, SCIM, audit logs) with the simplicity of a modern calendar app, so scaling secure scheduling across teams is seamless.

Can I restrict data access by team or department?Yes. Cal.com supports role-based access control (RBAC), sub-team structures, and domain enforcement so only authorized users can access or modify sensitive booking data.

Can I use my own branding and get a custom subdomain?Yes. You can host your scheduling pages on your own company.cal.com subdomain or fully white label Cal.com under your organization’s brand. Customize colors, logos, and booking pages to create a seamless, branded experience.

What support options are available for Enterprise customers?Enterprise plans include priority support, dedicated onboarding, and optional service-level agreements (SLAs) to ensure smooth implementation and ongoing success.

controls.name: Book a sales call with our team
Can I customize the AI phone calls?Yes, you can fully customize the language, tone, and prompts of the AI phone calls to align with your brand and scheduling needs.
Does Cal.ai work with my existing calendar?Yes, Cal.ai seamlessly integrates with your existing calendar and scheduling workflows on Cal.com, ensuring smooth automation of your booking process.
What happens if someone doesn’t answer the AI call?If a call is missed, Cal.ai can leave a voicemail, send a follow-up message, or retry the call, based on your predefined workflow settings.
Is Cal.ai available for all Cal.com plans?Yes, Cal.ai is available for all plans!

How does pricing work for Cal.ai? What is the cost per minute?Cal.ai pricing is based on credits, with each call consuming a set number of credits based on its length. The cost is 29 credits per minute, which equals $0.29 per minute.

How many credits are included in my current plan?Individuals don't get any credits included. Individuals have to purchase credits separately. Teams receive 750 credits per member per month. Organizations receive 1000 credits per member per month. Credits get renewed monthly. Usage updates in real time, and additional credits can be purchased anytime in your team settings. You can see your remaining Cal.ai credits in your Cal.com dashboard. Learn more here.
How can I buy more credits for Cal.ai?If you need additional Cal.ai credits, you can purchase them anytime through your Cal.com dashboard. Learn more here.
